newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka nets $10.9 mln by selling estate firms.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka nets $10.9 mln by selling estate firms.

text.p: Sri Lanka has raised nearly $11 million by slashing its holdings in privatised plantation firms, a senior government official said on Thursday.
"The process has raised over 640 million rupees ($10.9 million)," said an official from the Public Enterprise Reform Commission (PERC), the state arm that oversees privatisations.

PERC called for proposals from brokers in March on how best to reduce the balance government holding to one share from 3.8 million in six estate firms -- Kegalle Plantations, Agalawatte Plantations, Kelani Valley Plantations, Horana Plantations, Bogawantalawa Plantations and Kotgala Plantations.
The firms were privatised in 1995 and 1996 by selling 51 percent to a strategic investor and 20 percent to the public.
Ten percent was reserved for workers while the government retained 19 percent or 3.8 million shares in each firm.
The goverment is however keeping one 'golden' share in each firm for itself, which enables it to intervene in the event of mismanagement.
By Thursday the process of divestment had been completed in all firms except Kotagala Plantations.
